newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says it checked tankers in its waters.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says it checked tankers in its waters.

text.p: An Indonesian naval official said on Wednesday the navy had recently checked tankers and other vessels refuelling in Indonesian waters near Singapore, but denied checking vessels outside Indonesian limits.
Shipping sources in Singapore said on Tuesday Indonesian shipping authorities had boarded several tankers refuelling, or bunkering, outside Singapore port limits in international waters.
They said about 10 incidents had occurred so far in July in international waters west of Singapore and just outside the harbour limits.
"It is impossible that we checked tankers in international waters or in waters outside Indonesian limits," the naval official told Reuters by phone from Tanjung Pinang, close to Singapore.
He said a number of vessels had been checked recently in Indonesian waters.
"Our policy is to ask the tankers to anchor in a designated area (for bunkering). The area is in east Karimun," he said.

"We will continue to carry out government policy (on bunkering) to prevent possible illegal acitivity in our waters. We persuade the tankers to anchor in the designated area. We do not arrest them," he said.
The official said he had no other details.
